note: Committed government + major-industry funding and jobs pipelines, 5–10yr forward. The demand engine behind future migration and capital growth. STATUS matters — projects get delayed/cancelled (e.g. Whyalla H2), so each carries a status. Curated from government/industry sources; refresh at budget times (May federal, ~June states) or when a project's status changes. Sersi flags when this file is >90 days old.

markets.catalyst: Olympic venue build + Cross River Rail + Logan–Gold Coast faster rail; tipped to gentrify pre-2032.
markets.impact: Sustained Olympic + SEQ construction and interstate migration should drive above-average capital growth to 2032 and lift rents as workers arrive; broad SEQ land supply is the main brake, so favour established, supply-constrained pockets.

markets.catalyst: Entry ~$400k below Brisbane median with Olympic infrastructure + RAAF Amberley (largest RAAF base) + strong migration.
markets.impact: Defence (Amberley), health and logistics anchor a diversified job base — steady capital growth from a low entry point plus a stable rental floor from base personnel; new-build supply on the fringe caps the very outer estates.

markets.catalyst: Critical node on Inland Rail; Wellcamp precinct drawing Pacific National, Qube, Linfox. One of regional Australia's most diversified economies.
markets.impact: Freight/logistics + agribusiness + health make this low-volatility: expect steady, durable capital and rental growth rather than spikes; Wellcamp/Inland Rail lifts land values near the precinct.

markets.jobs: ~10,000 SA jobs at peak (4,000 build + 5,500 production)
markets.catalyst: Osborne submarine construction yard; Skills & Training Academy from 2028. Multi-decade defence demand feeding northern Adelaide.
markets.impact: ~10,000 multi-decade AUKUS jobs create structural rental demand and a new owner-occupier buyer pool — northern Adelaide should re-rate off a low base with strong long-run capital growth; key risk is build-timeline slippage pushing the demand out.

markets.jobs: Hydrogen 200+ construction; CopperString + minerals province; defence garrison
markets.catalyst: Townsville Hydrogen Hub (ops 2027) + CopperString 2032 (1,100km transmission to Mt Isa) + army garrison. Diversifying regional powerhouse.
markets.impact: A diversifying base (hydrogen + CopperString + garrison) converts a former single-industry town into resilient demand — capital and rental growth with the defence garrison stabilising rents; execution risk sits with the energy projects.

markets.catalyst: CQ Hydrogen Hub (ops 2027) + Alpha HPA high-purity alumina + SuperGrid transmission hub. Pivot from coal/LNG to green energy & metals.
markets.impact: 8,900+ energy/metals construction jobs can spike rents and lift prices sharply from a very low, high-yield base — but it's still transitioning off coal/LNG, so treat as higher-risk boom/bust, not a set-and-forget hold.

markets.jobs: Defence construction + US force posture; Middle Arm industry
markets.catalyst: National Defence Strategy 2026: harden northern bases over the decade; Middle Arm precinct (LNG + future clean energy/manufacturing). Very high yield, thin market.
markets.impact: $13–16B defence spend underwrites rental demand and capital growth in a very high-yield but thin market; historically volatile and illiquid, so size positions for the possibility of sharp reversals.

markets.jobs: Recent $65M / 200+ jobs (cold storage, steel fab, recycling)
markets.catalyst: Inland Rail + east–west junction; SAP drawing logistics. Small/thin market — higher risk.
markets.impact: Logistics jobs create localised rental demand and modest capital growth, but the market is small and illiquid — high sensitivity to a single project's timing; suits yield/'specufestor' risk appetite only.

markets.catalyst: CQ renewables + beef/agriculture base; affordable regional centre with yield.
markets.impact: Renewables corridor + agriculture support moderate, affordable, high-yield capital and rental growth; less explosive than the hydrogen towns but lower single-industry risk.

markets.catalyst: Hunter REZ + green hydrogen/ammonia, green metals, defence mfg — post-coal transition. $16M Uni New Energy Skills Hub.
markets.impact: Post-coal green-energy, green-metals and defence-manufacturing jobs sustain rental demand and capital growth in the outer Hunter; genuine diversification lowers the transition risk versus a pure coal town.

markets.jobs: SRL East+North up to 24,000 jobs across the economy
markets.catalyst: 90km orbital rail linking middle-ring hubs (Monash, Box Hill, Clayton). Station precincts to be rezoned for density — land-value uplift. First services ~2035.
markets.impact: 24,000 SRL jobs plus mandated station-precinct density = land-value uplift for houses on developable blocks near stations and rental demand from the new density — strong long-run capital growth, though inner-SE pricing already reflects some of it; buy near confirmed precincts.

markets.catalyst: Next SRL stage through Melbourne's north to the airport; earlier-cycle than SRL East. Watch station precincts.
markets.impact: Earlier-cycle SRL stage: station-precinct rezoning through the north hasn't been priced in yet, so this is the 'get in before the uplift' play — target houses on subdividable land near nominated stations.

markets.catalyst: Australia's first declared REZ; transmission approved 2025. Regional hub (Dubbo) drawing energy workforce + supply chains.
markets.impact: 5,000 REZ construction jobs and $20B of investment can spike regional rents and prices through the build phase; plan for demand to taper once construction peaks passes — a medium-term, not permanent, catalyst.

markets.catalyst: New underground metro doubling rail capacity Parramatta↔CBD; station precincts (Sydney Olympic Park, Five Dock, Burwood North) rezoned for density.
markets.impact: Sydney Metro West adds accessibility + precinct rezoning → land-value uplift and rental demand along the line (Sydney Olympic Park, Five Dock, Burwood North); strong but from an already-expensive base, so yields stay thin.

markets.catalyst: Continuous naval shipbuilding + nuclear-sub maintenance at Henderson; anchors Perth's southern corridor (Kwinana/Rockingham). Multi-decade demand.
markets.impact: ~10,000 shipbuilding/sub-maintenance jobs create structural, multi-decade rental and owner-occupier demand across Perth's southern corridor — a durable capital-growth anchor for Kwinana/Rockingham off a still-affordable base.

markets.funding: Fortescue green iron + 5 WA hydrogen hubs by 2030
markets.catalyst: Green 'pit-to-product' iron + Pilbara hydrogen hubs. High incomes, but commodity-cyclical + thin/expensive housing — treat with care.
markets.impact: High-income mining/energy jobs can spike rents and prices, but it's commodity-cyclical with thin, expensive housing — classic boom/bust; only for investors who actively manage the cycle and accept illiquidity.

markets.funding: $2.4B Cth+SA steelworks support (green H2 plant CANCELLED Feb 2025)
markets.catalyst: ⚠ Green-hydrogen power plant CANCELLED; steelworks in government administration seeking a buyer with a $2.4B support package. Single-industry, high risk — do not treat as a growth catalyst yet.
markets.impact: DOWNSIDE risk, not upside: with the green-hydrogen plant cancelled and the steelworks under administration, the town's economic base is uncertain — capital values and rents could fall if no buyer is secured. Avoid until resolved.

markets.catalyst: World-scale pumped hydro; still at refreshed-business-case stage (some uncertainty). Would inject a big regional construction workforce if it proceeds.
markets.impact: If Borumba proceeds it injects a large multi-year construction workforce → regional rental and capital-growth uplift; but it's still at business-case stage, so the catalyst is conditional — don't pay for it until it's committed.

markets.theme: Marinus Link + Battery of the Nation
markets.catalyst: Tas–Vic interconnector + pumped hydro ('Battery of the Nation'). Anchors NW Tasmania; cheapest capital-region-adjacent market in the country.
markets.impact: 1,400 Marinus jobs plus 'Battery of the Nation' lift rental demand and capital growth off the cheapest capital-adjacent base in the country — attractive entry + yield, with project-timeline the main risk.

markets.catalyst: Major pumped hydro; delayed & over budget but proceeding. Sustains a regional construction workforce near Cooma/Tumut.
markets.impact: Snowy 2.0's ~2,000 construction jobs sustain a regional rental base; the delays mean a drawn-out but ongoing demand tail rather than a sharp spike — modest, steady support.

watch.note: Huge catalyst — Western Sydney Airport opens 25 Oct 2026; Bradfield new city, 200,000 jobs by 2056, $25B infrastructure. But most house/townhouse stock is above $600k — monitor outer-SW pockets and off-the-plan townhouses.
Offshore-wind assembly port + advanced manufacturing candidate; already-run housing (mostly >$600k) but strong long-term jobs story.
